title: NY State Senate · District 13
area: Central Queens, including Jackson Heights, East Elmhurst, Corona and parts of Woodside and Elmhurst.

context.text: Incumbent Jessica Ramos lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. State Assemblymember Jessica González-Rojas won the primary with 47.9% of the vote (6,476 votes) against Ramos's 37.1% (5,024 votes) and Hiram Monserrate's 14.5% (1,966 votes); Ramos does not appear on the November general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Jessica González-Rojas
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assemblymember, District 34 (since 2021; not seeking re-election to the Assembly)

summary.text: Jessica González-Rojas is a NY State Assemblymember running for the open NY State Senate District 13 seat after defeating incumbent Jessica Ramos in the Democratic primary. She chairs the Assembly's Task Force on Women's Issues and previously spent 13 years in leadership at the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice.

background.text: Born and raised in Queens, New York.
Earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Boston University and a Master of Public Administration from New York University.
Worked as an adjunct professor at New York University and the City University of New York.
Spent 13 years in leadership positions at the National Latina Institute for Reproductive Justice before her election to the Assembly.
First elected to the NY State Assembly (District 34) in 2020, succeeding Michael DenDekker.

priorities.text: Cites health justice as a core passion, including securing funding for a health center in Jackson Heights.
Wants to continue the Assembly women's rights task force's agenda in the Senate, including universal child care and workforce development.
Says she is seeking a Senate seat to gain greater influence over state agency decisions and bring more resources to the neighborhoods she represents.

positions.summary: Sponsor of the state version of Medicare for All (New York Health Act) in the Assembly; campaigns on health justice, including local health-center funding.
Lists universal child care among the priorities she pursued through the Assembly's women's rights task force and plans to continue in the Senate.
Campaigns on immigrant advocacy and has said she is running partly to expand resources and protections for immigrant communities in her district.

record.text: Appointed Chair of the NY State Assembly's Task Force on Women's Issues by Speaker Carl Heastie for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the Assembly's Children and Families, Cities, Corporations Authorities and Commissions, Environmental Conservation, Health, and Social Services committees (2025-2026 session).

summary.text: John Healy is the Republican candidate for the open NY State Senate District 13 seat. A Queens native and President of the Sunnyside GOP Club, he previously ran for and lost a 2025 NYC Council race in District 26, which overlaps this Senate district.

background.text: A Queens native who serves as President of the Sunnyside GOP Club.
Ran for New York City Council District 26 (Western Queens) on the Republican and Conservative Party lines in 2025 and lost the general election.

priorities.text: In his prior Council campaign, an endorsing club described his focus on Western Queens quality-of-life issues, including "safer and cleaner streets, improved quality of life, and preservation of the character of our communities."
priorities.quote: safer and cleaner streets, improved quality of life, and preservation of the character of our communities
